answer: Copper-Weighted Neighbor Entropy. Each agent's influence is scaled by the diversity of its inbound links, measured as entropy over the source clusters those links come from; a crystal of tightly self-linked identities contributes near-zero entropy and thus near-zero weight. To gain real influence, an attacker must recruit genuinely independent clusters, paying their acquisition cost per sybil. A glacier-slow decay halves link entropy over weeks, forcing sustained spend to hold rank.
